retrieved.text: # Lecture 3: Model evaluation We hold out a test set so we can estimate how the model performs on data it has never seen. Evaluating on the training data rewards memorization and hides overfitting. Cross-validation splits the training data into k folds, trains on k-1 folds and validates on the remaining fold, rotating so every fold is used once for validation; the average score is a more stable estimate than a single split. Accuracy can mislead on imbalanced classes, so we also report precision, recall and the F1 score.

To classify a new point, find the k training points closest to it (usually by Euclidean distance) and take a majority vote of their labels. There is no training phase beyond storing the data; the cost is paid at prediction time.

from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier
X, y = load_iris(return_X_y=True)
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=42, stratify=y)
acc = KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=3).fit(X_train, y_train).score(X_test, y_test)
print("k=3 test accuracy:", round(acc, 3))
